teams.heading: World Rugby report names Fiji among 10 countries facing climate threat
teams.body: Climate change could leave rugby unplayable on more days, damage stadiums and pitches and heighten risks to players and spectators, a new World Rugby report warns. Fiji are among the 10 countries the report identifies as facing projected impacts, though today's coverage does not set out the specific findings for the islands. It lands as the Flying Fijians, beaten 15-43 by Ireland and winless in five Nations Championship tests, prepare to face Italy in Udine on Saturday.

lead.why: It is the only new item that is about Fiji itself rather than Italy's or Ireland's preparations.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick welcomes back Furbank, Chessum and Atkinson before All Blacks test
teams.body: Full-back George Furbank, vice-captain Ollie Chessum and inside centre Seb Atkinson all missed the 78-15 win over Japan — Furbank and Atkinson with groin problems, Chessum with a shoulder injury — but were named in last Sunday's 36-man squad for Saturday's test against New Zealand. That is a boost for England head coach Steve Borthwick. Furbank had shone against Australia in his first England appearance in two years. England tighthead Joe Heyes says the side now have a taste for beating the All Blacks after last year's 33-19 win.

teams.heading: Kalvin Gourgues expected to take over France's goal-kicking against Argentina
teams.body: The Toulouse centre is in line for the tee on Saturday, Rugbyrama reports, which would make him France's third goal-kicker in three Nations Championship matches. Thomas Ramos is out with a thigh injury, Romain Ntamack hurt his shoulder against Fiji, scrum-half Maxime Lucu — 3/4 against South Africa — looks bound for the bench and Matthieu Jalibert is being spared kicking after recent right quadriceps trouble. Gourgues landed his only attempt against Fiji; his one other professional stint with the tee brought a perfect 5/5 for Toulouse against Perpignan in January.

lead.why: A fresh, match-pinned selection call for Saturday's Argentina test, ahead of a backward-looking reaction to last week's clearout.

teams.heading: Gus McCarthy to captain Ireland XV against Fijian Latui in Cork
teams.body: Leinster hooker Gus McCarthy and Ulster back-row David McCann have returned from senior camp to start for the Ireland XV against Fijian Latui at Cork's Virgin Media Park on Friday. McCarthy, one of eight Ireland-capped players in the squad, packs down between Alex Usanov and Kieran Brookes. Joey Carbery partners Leinster scrum-half Fintan Gunne at half-back, and capped trio Jeremy Loughman, Jack Aungier and Paul Boyle are named among the replacements.

lead.why: A fresh Ireland selection event, preferred over a TV listing, the already-reported Prendergast story and a pundit's verdict.

teams.heading: Italy schedule children's ward visit and war memorial tribute around Fiji test
teams.body: The Italian Rugby Federation's programme for Saturday's Fiji test in Udine began with an Azzurri delegation scheduled to visit the paediatric oncology ward at Santa Maria della Misericordia hospital on Wednesday. Friday brings a tribute at the Redipuglia war memorial to Italy's First World War dead and the launch of a pink Gilbert ball promoting breast-cancer prevention, with €10 from each sale going to the Aviano cancer centre. On matchday, federation president Andrea Duodo opens BlackOut, a conference on head injuries.

lead.why: It is the only new Italy item not already covered, since the TV and series-record angle ran this morning.

teams.heading: Gregor Townsend hails Scotland's defence after Australia 'arm wrestle' at Murrayfield
teams.body: Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend rated Sunday's 15-12 Nations Championship win over Australia as a defensive high point: "Defensively, that's one of the best performances I've seen in the last couple of years." It followed a heavy defeat by New Zealand in which Scotland failed to score a second-half point. Townsend said keeping the Wallabies out of Scotland's 22 was a lesson learned from that game. The win held only after Scotland's Darcy Graham bundled Australia full-back Tom Wright into touch with the clock in the red.

lead.why: The NEW item and the injury news have both already run, so the head coach's post-match verdict on the Australia win is the strongest Scotland story the reader hasn't seen.

teams.heading: Wales set to recall Wainwright, Carter and Adams for Australia test
teams.body: Head coach Steve Tandy is weighing changes for Saturday's Australia test after the 35-28 win over New Zealand, WalesOnline reports. Back-rower Aaron Wainwright, who missed that game with a minor leg injury, is expected to start at No. 8 if he comes through training. Lock Ben Carter could replace Adam Beard, who is nursing an apparent shoulder injury. Flyer Josh Adams, left out for his heavy load, looks set to return. Flanker James Botham is due to become a father this week, with Alex Mann starting if he is unavailable.

lead.why: Fresh selection news for the Australia test beats a second retelling of Tandy's post-match reaction.

teams.heading: Bautista Bernasconi reportedly ruled out of Pumas' France test with muscle injury
teams.body: The Benetton hooker, who scored a first-half try in last Saturday's 19-14 win over Italy in Genoa, hurt a muscle in that match and has been left out of the Pumas camp in Paris, according to Argentine outlet Salida de 22 and others. The severity has not been reported. Fellow hookers Ignacio Ruiz and Leonel Oviedo are also injured. Julián Montoya, who missed the Italy game with concussion, appears to have cleared his latest checks.

lead.why: A fresh injury ruling Argentina's try-scoring hooker out of Saturday's test is a material new development, not a retelling.

teams.heading: Tom Hooper jokes about lacing Exeter teammate Dafydd Jenkins's coffee before Wales
teams.body: Wallabies forward Tom Hooper, back from a shoulder injury, is meeting his Exeter Chiefs teammate Dafydd Jenkins for coffee before Saturday's test against Wales. He joked he "might slip some laxatives in his coffee." Jenkins, a Wales forward, matched the Test record of 38 tackles held by France's Thierry Dusautoir in last weekend's 35-28 win over the All Blacks. Hooper reckons he "might have to run at him 39 times so he can break the record". Utility back Ben Donaldson promised to keep challenging the line under the Principality Stadium roof.

lead.why: It is the only fresh Australia-camp story, with player quotes a fan would pass on, while the top two items are Wales team news.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones shoulders blame after Hockings' first-minute red card at Twickenham
teams.body: Japan lock Hockings was shown yellow for a dangerous tackle in the passage of play that produced England's opening try in the first minute. The card was later upgraded to red. Japan then conceded five tries in roughly 20 minutes on the way to a 15-78 defeat to England, 13 tries in all. Head coach Eddie Jones said in his post-match interview that he takes full responsibility for the result. Writing in the Guardian, Gerard Meagher noted that Japan were a man down before they had touched the ball.

lead.why: It is Japan's own post-match story: the first-minute red card that shaped the rout and Jones accepting the blame, which has not yet been reported here.

teams.heading: Justin Marshall partly blames Mo'unga selection for 'one-dimensional' All Blacks against Wales
teams.body: Former All Blacks scrum-half Justin Marshall told the GBRANZ podcast that Richie Mo'unga, starting at No. 10 with Damian McKenzie rested, plays "flat to the line" and that the side missed McKenzie's "sweeping arc runs" in Saturday's 35-28 defeat in Cardiff, a first loss to Wales in 73 years. Three first-half tries became one after the break as the attack grew too direct; Marshall said there were no block plays and no use of the field's width to stretch the Welsh defence.

lead.why: The freshest New Zealand-centred item, a named pundit's verdict on a selection call behind Saturday's defeat in Cardiff.

teams.heading: Banned Rassie Erasmus invites Springbok fans to watch Ireland test with him
teams.body: Barred from the Aviva Stadium for Saturday's Nations Championship test against Ireland, the Springbok head coach will watch from his hotel room on laptop camera, with adults signing up at watchwithrassie.com to join him. "Can sit and moan or make the best of it," Erasmus wrote on X. Fans watch on their own televisions while he reads out some of their messages. World Rugby banned him for six matches over his criticism of officials after the 19-21 defeat to France; he and SA Rugby have requested a hearing.

lead.why: Erasmus hosting a public watch-along of the Ireland test while banned is a fresh South Africa event, separate from the ban and abuse stories already run.
